summary: This is a sound, rules-clean redesign of the chunked align. It parallelises over experts and removes the serial single-CTA bottleneck that made _align_chunked_kernel 16.5/29.2 us. The realistic gain is 1.5-2.5% per verify shape and about 0.5% on the headline, so the run will almost certainly be classified as neutral. Judge it on the new kernel row against the four removed rows in top_kernels, and fix the [1024,32] one-hot register blow-up before building.
justification: Mechanism: at bs=128/256, master's else-branch runs at::native index_elementwise (3.2/3.3 us), the align wrapper's unrolled_elementwise fill (~2.8 us), moe_align_block_size_kernel (~2.7 us) and count_and_sort (~1.8-2.6 us). That is about 10.5/11.5 us against 333/470 us of shape time. Marlin is 94-95% of each verify shape (316/490 us vs floors of 101/109 us), so this area is capped at ~3.1%/~2.4% per shape even for a free kernel. With a 3-5 us kernel and ~1 us of saved graph-node cost (LESSONS: ~0.3 us per single Triton launch node), expect ~6-8 us, i.e. ~2% at bs=128 and ~1.5% at bs=256. Over the 6 equally weighted loads that is ~0.5-0.6% on the geomean, inside the +-1.5% CI and the 1.5-2.5% per-shape drift. The expected shapes and directions are right: faster at bs=128/256, flat at bs<=32, where _align_small is byte-identical and serves as the in-run drift control. The design parallelism is plausible. Each of the 33 programs reads only 2-8 KB of ids, and pass 2 needs only a 1-D match mask and cumsum, unlike the chunked kernel's [CHUNK,32] cumsum. Weakest link 1 (the argument): the claim that 'the removed node overhead is real' rests on the chunked run's paired ratios, bs=128 1.403 vs 1.375 (+2.0%) and bs=256 1.301 vs 1.314 (-1.0%). Both are inside drift, and the Marlin row itself moved 316->337 and 490->462 us between those runs. So the hidden ~6 us node saving the expected section leans on is unproven; budget ~1 us. Weakest link 2 (the build): CHUNK=1024 with num_warps=4 makes the [1024,32] int32 one-hot 256 live values per thread per temporary, 4x the chunked kernel's 64. That will likely spill and could push the kernel past the ~6 us break-even. Use CHUNK=512 with num_warps=8, or CHUNK=256 with num_warps=4 (64 per thread), or tl.histogram over remote-remapped ids if this Triton version supports a mask. Also: each program's own block_experts range can span up to cdiv(M, BSM) blocks (8 at bs=128 BSM 16 and at bs=256 BSM 32; more at skewed-128), so it needs a loop or a power-of-2 arange sized for that bound. The spec leaves this unstated. Extract seg_start[e] and count[e] with a where+sum over the expert axis, and cast the bool match mask to int32 before tl.cumsum.
confounders: marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: sets BSM=16 at bs=128 and 32 at bs=256/257. That fixes cap, n_blocks, the padding width and each expert's block count, so it shifts the new kernel's own time slightly (well under 1 us). It does not change what Marlin receives, so it does not confound attribution of the removed align rows. Without it, BSM would be 48/64, and PAD_BLOCK=64 would matter more.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack / triton-map-align-small-m-port: same area and same design family, but gated at <=32 tokens. Those shapes are this run's byte-identical control, not a confounder. Latent hazard: _align_small_kernel still uses tl.arange(0, BSM) unpadded, which is safe only because its BSM is <=16.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: no timing confound at the target shapes. bs>=32 still calls fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum with slot_expert_ids=local_ids, and silu_and_mul uses expert_ids=local_ids. Program 32's local_ids must be exactly -1 for remote routes and int32 contiguous, as on master. This is a correctness dependency, not an attribution one.

sglang-marlin-path-parity: provides the base pipeline and the 32-expert capacity contract (cap = n + 32*(BSM-1), n_blocks = cdiv(cap, BSM), sentinel n). It does not interact beyond the sizes the kernel must reproduce.
interference: No companion is warranted. Nothing landed sits between the change and its measurement. The four removed rows and the one added row are directly visible in top_kernels, and Triton kernel times reproduce within ~1% between runs, so the kernel-level comparison is interpretable from this single run. The headline and per-shape ratios are dominated by Marlin drift, which no A/B companion fixes. An ab-revert of block-m-two-smaller would change only BSM and the padding cost and could not flip the reading. A CHUNK/num_warps ab-tune is a follow-up to choose from this run's kernel row, not a disambiguator. Decision rule for the harvest: merge by hand if the log shows the self-check with 0 mismatches for T in {33..257}, _align_parallel_kernel at or below (sum of removed rows - ~2 us) at both verify shapes, and the bs=128/256 paired ratios at or above master's, even if classify says neutral. If the kernel row exceeds ~8 us at bs=256, gate it to bs<=128 or shrink CHUNK in a follow-up.
open_questions: The new kernel's own time at bs=256 (n=2048, 2 chunks x 2 passes per program at CHUNK=1024). Check the compile log or register report for spills at [1024,32] int32 with 4 warps. If the build keeps CHUNK=1024, consider num_warps=8.

skewed-128: the busiest expert can receive up to M routes (128, so 8 blocks at BSM 16). Confirm the per-program block_experts and route-store loops are bounded by a runtime loop, not a fixed small arange.
Does this image's Triton support tl.histogram with a mask? It would replace the one-hot entirely in pass 1 (map remote routes to bin 32 of a 64-bin histogram if there is no mask).

Prepare-time compile: four BSM variants plus 6 more self-check T values. Expected seconds, well inside 300 s. Confirm every BSM variant (16/32/48/64) compiled before trusting the timings, given the chunked kernel's arange history.
With moe at 2 checks left today, the expected classify outcome is neutral (about 0.5% headline). Is the second check better kept for a follow-up tune of this kernel than for a held item?
